p: When it's dark by teatime and the kids are bouncing off the walls, an indoor obstacle course is the perfect antidote. A session after school or on a gloomy weekend afternoon can do wonders for everyone's mood, and the kids tend to sleep like logs afterwards.

Stockton has a special place in railway history, too. The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in 1825 and is often described as the world's first public railway to use steam locomotives, and the town marked its 200th anniversary in 2025. Train-mad children will enjoy tracing the story around the area.

Preston Park Museum and Grounds, just south of the town, is a family favourite. Its recreated Victorian street lets you step back in time, and the surrounding parkland is great for a walk or a play. Ropner Park, a Victorian park closer to the centre, has a lake, a bandstand and plenty of space.

For nature, RSPB Saltholme, near the Tees, is a wetland reserve with easy trails, hides and a visitor centre overlooking the water. It's a great spot for spotting birds and letting the kids run off any remaining energy. The striking Transporter Bridge in nearby Middlesbrough is also worth seeing from the riverside, even just for a photo. It's a proper piece of Teesside engineering, and a good way to end a day that started with your own feats of balance and strength.
